title: When the Landfall Falls
premise: Quentin Kavanagh has spent a decade erasing themselves from their famous archaeologist mother's shadow, working remote river surveys where nobody asks questions. When an unprecedented low tide exposes a sea cave on the Karst Coast—a cave local legend says holds the drowned archive of a vanished trading people—Quentin's discovery draws the attention of a salvage syndicate, a grieving historian, and, worst of all, their estranged mother, who arrives claiming the cave matches her life's unfinished theory. As monsoon season bears down, Quentin realizes the cave's true treasure is a map of the river's forbidden headwaters, and that whoever reaches the source first will control the region's water rights and rewrite its history. Racing upstream through collapsing gorges and buried villages, Quentin must decide whether inheritance is something you escape or something you carry—and in the flooded chamber at the source, they choose to give the archive to the descendants of the vanished people rather than to academia or profit, finally making peace with the mother they leave behind on the riverbank.
about_author: Jude Eriksen is a former river guide who spent six seasons running freight through monsoon country before turning to fiction. Their writing blends field-hardened adventure with quiet meditations on what families bury and what tides return.

chapters.title: The Lowest Tide in Living Memory
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. Working a routine coastal survey, Quentin notices the tide has dropped impossibly far, exposing black rock never seen before. A fisherman warns them some holes are meant to stay shut. The beat is wary curiosity—the first crack in Quentin's carefully invisible life.

chapters.title: What the Cave Keeps
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. Quentin enters the cave alone and finds carved ledger walls, sealed jars, and a stone door bearing a spiral sigil matching a pendant their mother wore. They photograph nothing and tell no one—but someone's boat is anchored offshore. The beat is dread disguised as triumph.

chapters.title: People Who Ask Questions
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. In the port town of Sallow's Reach, Quentin is approached by Vess Odumbe, a historian chasing her grandfather's lost expedition, and by polite men from the Meridian Salvage Group who already know Quentin's name. The beat is claustrophobia: invisibility failing on all fronts.

chapters.title: A Letter in Her Handwriting
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. A letter arrives: Dr. Marion Kavanagh is coming, convinced the cave proves her thirty-year theory about the Riverfolk archive. Quentin burns it, then can't stop reading the ashes' memory. The beat is old anger resurfacing as grief.

chapters.title: The Syndicate Makes an Offer
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. Meridian's fixer, Corliss Hale, offers Quentin a consulting fee large enough to disappear forever—in exchange for the cave's location. Quentin refuses badly, revealing more than intended. The beat is self-disgust and the realization the choice was never really offered.

chapters.title: Mother, Arriving
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. Marion steps off the ferry unannounced, older and sharper than Quentin remembered. Their first conversation is a duel of archaeology and avoidance until Marion mentions the spiral sigil—and Quentin's childhood pendant. The beat is two people excavating each other.

chapters.title: Vess's Grandfather's Map
chapters.summary: POV Vess Odumbe. Shifting POV, Vess shares her grandfather's journal: his 1961 expedition traced the river upstream seeking the archive's source and never returned. The journal includes a fragmentary route through the gorges. The beat is reluctant alliance forming over shared obsession.

chapters.title: Someone Has Been in the Cave
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. Returning at night, Quentin finds the ledger walls chiseled, jars broken, and fresh drill marks on the stone door. Meridian got there first—or wants Quentin to think so. The beat is violation, and the dawning certainty that the door must be opened from the source side.

chapters.title: Upstream Is the Only Way
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. Deciphering the ledgers, Quentin and Marion realize the cave is an outflow: the true archive lies at the river's source, in country closed by both law and legend. Monsoon landfall is eleven days out. The beat is commitment—Quentin chooses the river over hiding.

chapters.title: The Gorge Road
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. The expedition—Quentin, Marion, Vess—pushes upriver by boat and foot through narrowing gorges while Meridian's crew shadows them. A rockslide nearly kills Marion; Quentin saves her without a word. The beat is grudging tenderness under pressure.

chapters.title: The Village That Remembers
chapters.summary: POV Vess. The team reaches Kesh-Taru, a river village whose elders are living descendants of the Riverfolk. An elder, Ama Sefu, recognizes the spiral sigil and tells them the source is a grave, not a vault. The beat is humility—the explorers realize they may be trespassers.

chapters.title: Ama Sefu's Price
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. Ama Sefu agrees to guide them only if anything found at the source belongs to the Riverfolk's heirs—not museums, not companies, not mothers. Marion hesitates; Quentin signs before she does. The beat is Quentin choosing a different inheritance than the one they were raised on.

chapters.title: Meridian Closes In
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. Hale's crew overtakes them at the rapids, seizing supplies and taking Vess's journal. Hale offers one last deal: bring me the source, and everyone walks away. Quentin lies to his face for the first time convincingly. The beat is cold resolve hardening into strategy.

chapters.title: The Buried Ferry Town
chapters.summary: POV Marion. POV shifts to Marion navigating an abandoned ferry town drowned by an old dam, where she confesses why she let Quentin go: she chose the dig over the hospital room years ago. The beat is confession without absolution, and Quentin listening anyway.

chapters.title: Landfall Warning
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. Radio reports confirm the monsoon will make landfall in three days, days ahead of forecast. Ama Sefu says the river will rise faster than any forecast. The team must reach the source now or lose the window for a year. The beat is the clock becoming a character.

chapters.title: The Forbidden Source
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. At dawn they reach the headwater spring beneath a natural limestone dome: the true archive, intact, a whole civilization's memory in resin-sealed chambers. Behind them, Hale's crew arrives armed. The beat is awe interrupted by threat.

chapters.title: Standoff at the Spring
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. Hale demands the archive; Marion stalls him with scholarship, Vess with law, Ama Sefu with witness. When Hale's explosives man moves toward the dome, Quentin triggers a controlled collapse sealing the approach tunnel, trapping both sides inside. The beat is desperate courage with irreversible cost.

chapters.title: Water Rising
chapters.summary: POV Vess. Sealed in with the storm-fed spring rising fast, the group must evacuate the fragile archive through a submerged sump only the Riverfolk records describe. Ama Sefu reads the old glyphs aloud; Quentin dives the sump to set the guide line. The beat is terror transmuted into trust.

chapters.title: What Quentin Carries Out
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. On the last dive, Quentin could take the master ledger for themselves—the proof, the fame, the end of being nobody. Instead they carry out a child's recording tablet belonging to Ama Sefu's lineage and leave the rest. The beat is the book's thesis made flesh: inheritance means stewardship.

chapters.title: Landfall
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. The monsoon hits as they descend the swollen river, the source flooding behind them, Hale's crew scattered and his claim drowned in legal ambiguity. On the gorge rim, soaked and half-broken, the survivors watch the valley disappear under brown water. The beat is exhausted, earned survival.

chapters.title: Giving It Back
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. Weeks later in Kesh-Taru, the recovered tablets are formally returned to the Riverfolk descendants, with Vess documenting provenance and Marion signing away her claim publicly. Mother and child stand apart in the crowd, neither apologizing, both changed. The beat is reconciliation without erasure.

chapters.title: When the Landfall Falls
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. A year on, Quentin leads a new survey—this time hired by the Riverfolk council itself, the tide-predicting instruments theirs to read. At the coast, the sea cave breathes with the tide, its door left as found. The final beat is belonging: Quentin stops being invisible by choosing to be seen, on their own terms.
